fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The LORD says it plainly: “…one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) The one He raised up is the one calling on His name. That's the detail the statement asks about, and you caught it.

Reading out a rulebook sounds official, I'll give you that. But the LORD doesn't ask for laws at all. He asks them to “…tell us what will happen.” and to “Tell the former things…” too. (Isaiah 41:22) The test is about what they can tell, both what's past and what's coming.
That's the verdict, baker. The LORD says, “Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value.” (Isaiah 41:24) Plain and short. I've heard longer rulings on a burnt batch.
Not quite, friend, and I've gotten turned around in a dark drawer myself, so I feel you. The verse says “…from the north…” and “…from the east…” (Isaiah 41:25) South and west don't show up at all.
True, baker. The LORD says, “when I ask them, they have nothing to say.” (Isaiah 41:28) He asks, and the idols give Him silence. I've had a quiet oven act more helpful than that.
Easy one to flip, friend, but the verse is clear. The LORD says, “when I ask them, they have nothing to say.” (Isaiah 41:28) The idols stay silent. So the statement is true.

That's the word, baker. The LORD says, “See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.” (Isaiah 41:29) He calls the idols a delusion, and He says their images are as empty as the wind.
